key_insight: AI and machine learning are reshaping chemical engineering by combining data-driven prediction with first-principles models across scales, from atoms to full processes.
engineering_relevance: The main impact is more robust design and operation of materials, reactors, separations, and industrial systems through physics-informed, hybrid decision tools.
method: Integrate ML with first-principles, conservation laws, and thermodynamic constraints
Apply AI across multiscale domains: simulations, materials discovery, transport, separations, and process systems
Use hybrid frameworks to improve extrapolation, interpretability, and model lifecycle management
evidence_signal: The abstract summarizes representative applications across multiple chemical engineering domains and emphasizes improved robustness through physics-informed integration rather than a single benchmark result.
watch_item: A key challenge is ensuring reliable performance under data scarcity and out-of-distribution conditions while maintaining interpretability and consistency with physical laws.
paper_title: Atoms to Processes: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Chemical Engineering
